text:
maria: Hey team — escalated from Rahul (customer). They saw short 429 bursts for a tenant even though org-level burst pool showed plenty of credits. Happens when many tiny requests (50–200 token calls) hit different API keys in same org. Rahul: saw 429s for ~10s window, then everything recovered. We have request IDs and timeline.
rahul: Posting repro steps: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-org-xyz' -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "input":"hi"}' run loop 600x across 50 sub-keys. Observed failures around iteration 320-330.
maria: Attached logs: 
```
2026-06-03T12:05:21Z req_id=abc123 key=subkey-47 status=429 reason=burst_quota_exhausted pool_remaining=1200
2026-06-03T12:05:22Z req_id=abc124 key=subkey-12 status=200 tokens=45
2026-06-03T12:05:22Z req_id=abc125 key=subkey-05 status=429 reason=route_bucket_empty
```
maria: Note: org pool_remaining 1200 at same time, but some sub-keys show route_bucket_empty. Looks like fragmentation of credits into per-route buckets with rounding/truncation.
devon: Can you confirm whether customer is on Dedicated or Hosted? Also paste the exact model and concurrency.
rahul: Hosted (pay-as-you-go), model redwood-13b, per-request concurrency low, tests were parallelized from 100 processes.
kayla: Hitting fragmentation makes sense — we have per-route micro-buckets + fractional refill. We recently changed fractional_refill default off for hosted; that could cause small buckets to drain faster and not receive fractional top-ups until full interval.
devon: If that's the case, smoothing won't appear because each subkey has min_bucket_size=1 credit granularity and refill_interval=60s. Small rapid requests across many keys can exhaust route buckets while org pool still has credits waiting to be redistributed.
maria: Repro steps request from eng-runtime: can you run a synthetic with headers to force route-throughput logging?
devon: On it. Also attaching quick mitigation: increase burst_smoothing.window_ms to 10000 and enable fractional_refill:true on the org pool — this will allow sub-route buckets to accumulate fractional credits and reduce per-key 429s.
rahul: Is that something we can toggle from console? We need guidance for customer self-serve.
kayla: For Hosted customers, fractional_refill is currently behind a feature flag. Ops can flip it for the org temporarily. Short-term workaround: reduce test concurrency or consolidate requests to fewer sub-keys (reuse subkeys) so fewer buckets are contending.
maria: Suggested message to customer: "We're investigating per-key bucket fragmentation. We're enabling fractional refill for your org and increasing smoothing window to reduce 429s during short fan-out bursts. Expect improvement within 1 minute after change. If you can't reduce concurrency, we can route traffic via a single service key to avoid fragmentation."
devon: Logging note for engineering: add metric route_bucket_fragmentation_ratio and log fractional_remaining with pool_refill_timestamp. Also capture request_size_histogram (token footprints) to correlate small requests.
kayla: Filed ENGRT-1284 for an ETA on changing default fractional_refill for Hosted. Short-term: ops toggle planned in 15 min.
quota-bot: org/org-xyz fractional_refill toggled -> true by ops@redwood at 2026-06-03T12:11:05Z
rahul: Thank you — we'll rerun the test now and report back.
maria: Follow-up request: please capture a sample of 20 request ids from the failed window and send to eng with timeline. That helps trace token accounting.
rahul: Will do, sending via DM.
